body.p: Claims 1-20 are pending. Claims 1, 8, and 15 are independent.

Applicant amends claims 1, 8, and 15 to improve their form and expedite prosecution. No new matter is added. Applicant does not concede patentability of the subject matter encompassed by the claims before this amendment over the art cited by the Examiner. Applicant reserves the right to pursue claims in one or more continuing applications, including additional claims and claims capturing the subject matter encompassed by the claims before this amendment. At least 1 49 of the Specification supports this amendment.
Applicant's Representative: Michael Brooke Examiner: Kira Nguyen

Applicant thanks Examiner Nguyen for interviewing on 18 September 2024, during which the rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102 was discussed. The Examiner indicated that the proposed amendment may overcome the 102 rejection. Further search/consideration is required. No agreement was reached regarding allowability.
Claims 1-20 are rejected on the ground of nonstatutory double patenting as allegedly unpatentable over claims 1-20 of U.S. Patent No. 11,801,832.
Without conceding the propriety of this rejection, Applicant submits a terminal disclaimer with this Response.
Claims 1-20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) as allegedly anticipated by U.S. Patent Application Pub. No. 2019/0137290 to Levy et al. (LEVY). Applicant traverses this rejection.

Without acquiescing in this rejection, Applicant amended the claims as discussed in the interview. Therefore, Applicant submits LEVY does not anticipate claims 1-20. Accordingly, Applicant requests that the examiner reconsider and withdraw this rejection.
Applicant submits that the claims are in condition for allowance.

Applicant submits that this response overcomes the Examiner's rejections. Applicant's silence as to assertions or requirements in the Office Action that may apply to such assertions (e.g., whether a reference constitutes prior art, reasons to modify a reference or to combine references, assertions as to dependent claims, allegations of Official Notice, etc.) is not a concession by Applicant that such assertions are accurate or such requirements have been met. Accordingly, Applicant reserves the right to dispute such assertions.
If the Examiner believes a telephone conference would expedite the prosecution of this application, please telephone Michael Brooke at the number listed below.
